description: We are here to build a health monitoring software for astronauts in space mission.
summary:
Vela BioTelemetry is an autonomous crew health monitoring and countermeasure console built for astronauts on long-duration space missions. It integrates telemetry across five NASA Human Research Program domains—cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, space radiation, immune/cabin environment, and behavioral health—into one diagnostic interface.
To address the challenge of enabling astronauts to spot and act on physiological changes themselves, the software compares live indicators and 142-day longitudinal trends against each crew member's pre-flight baseline. Astronauts can monitor real-time ECG and force-plate bone loading during resistive leg exercises on the ARED bay, run a 5-trial Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) reaction test, check for ocular distortion (SANS) using an Amsler grid, and simulate hazardous events like elevated cabin CO₂ or solar particle flares. A built-in clinical evaluation engine translates detected drifts into prioritized, step-by-step countermeasure checklists and exportable Flight Surgeon handover reports.
As missions venture beyond low Earth orbit, communication delays and isolation shift medical responsibility onto the crew. Vela BioTelemetry empowers astronauts with clear, self-guided diagnostics and actionable countermeasures to protect bone density, cardiovascular fitness, radiation safety, and cognitive readiness.
